events.title: On Campus Service: Old Growth Forest
events.description:
Want to serve without travelling to far? Passionate about environmental conservation? 

The rare old-growth urban forest near Lane Stadium on the campus of Virginia Tech covers approximately 11.5 acres. It contains over 250 large trees, including dozens of white oak trees that have been estimated by scientists to be over 300 years old. 

Work alongside Master Naturalists to remove invasive species on Sundays and Tuesdays from 3 PM to 5 PM! Volunteers should bring GLOVES, wear LONG SLEEVES and LONG PANTS and CLOSED TOE SHOES as well as snacks, water, bug repellent. 

Sundays - Meet at the southwestern corner of the Woods at the end of Green Street
Tuesdays - VT Engage parking lot at the north end of the OGF (417 Clay Street)

Sign up here!

events.title: WORMWOOD, or dances for the demon AI in the organic apocalypse
events.description:
WORMWOOD is an Dance+AI performance exploring the limits and possibilities of artificial intelligence in live dance. The work explores the potential of Large Language Models (LLM) in real-time dance observation and analysis, and the poetic and literary interpretations of an AI witnessing human movement. The piece paints a portrait of a man enthralled to Wormwood, a digital creature-system that blurs the boundaries of machine, friend, oracle, and parasite. 

FREE! (Registration required)

Performed & Choreographed by: Scotty Hardwig (School of Performing Arts)
Coding & Visual/Sonic Interfaces: Zach Duer (School of Visual Arts)

Immediately following the performance: Q&A with the Performers

events.title: KickStart
events.description:
What is KickStart?
KickStart is a dedicated opportunity for teams in the Apex Incubator to share updates on their startup progress as they move through key milestones in the Incubator roadmap. The event is also open to students and faculty who want to observe, learn about the startups, and connect with participating teams.
What is the purpose?
KickStart helps teams communicate where they are, what they’ve accomplished, and what they need to move forward. For teams facing funding-related barriers, it also provides an opportunity to request funding that can help unlock their next milestone.
What can you expect?
During KickStart, teams will:
Share updates on their startup progress and milestones achieved.
Present their next milestone or priority on the Incubator roadmap.
Identify challenges or funding barriers that may be blocking progress.
Explain what funding is needed for and how it will be used to advance their startup.
Connect with students, faculty, and others interested in their work.
Who should attend?
Apex Incubator teams, students, and faculty are welcome! Incubator teams can present their progress and funding needs, while other attendees can observe the presentations, learn about startups being built at Apex, and connect with the teams.

events.title: Short Course: Walk in the Light while There is Light
events.description:
Russian literature, and especially the work of Leo Tolstoy—known for his lengthy novels War and Peace and Anna Karenina—can be intimidating. A master of expressing the human condition, with all its joys and, perhaps more famously, its tragedies, Tolstoy was also a deeply religious writer working within a complex and rich Christian tradition.

Written mostly later in his life, these readable and engaging short stories raise some of the most difficult questions of the Christian life. The title story, Walk in the Light While There Is Light, explores the parallel lives of two men in Tarsus during the time of the early church. Along with other short stories from the same series, it provides opportunities to explore the roles of faith, reason, and love in the lives of those who follow Christ.

Meeting every Tuesday in September, the group will often focus on just one short story each week. While the discussion will build with each new story, you are welcome to join as you are able! Feel free to reach out to Connie Bayliss with any questions.

Course readings: Walk in the Light while There is Light and Where Love is, There God is Also, two collections of several short stories by Tolstoy, both compiled by Lawrence Jordan. Additional readings drawing from Tolstoy's longer works, as well as those by other authors, may be shared and read during course meetings.

Copies of the books will be provided by the BSC for those who RSVP!

events.title: Venture Builders Workshop(Jobs Process & Buying Ecosystem)
events.description:
What are Venture Builders Workshops?
Come meet other students interested in launching new ventures and develop new skills with Venture Builder’s Workshops.  Our workshops cover a variety of topics, including the exploration of customer problems through gathering first-person data, formation of actionable startup hypotheses, and how to validate those hypotheses through lightweight, technology-driven experiments—ultimately setting up our student entrepreneurs to build evidence-based ventures.
Not a student founder?  No problem. Whether you’re actively building a venture, are interested in joining a team, or just curious about entrepreneurship, all are welcome! 
What purpose do these workshops fulfill?
Each workshop connects to a specific incubator module, with an emphasis on learning concepts by putting them into practice, giving students the opportunity to explore key concepts, ask questions, and better understand the material.
What will this workshop be about?
This workshop further hones in on Finding Your Customer, with a deeper focus on understanding the Job Process and Buying Ecosystem surrounding your initial customer profile.
During this workshop, you will:
Examine the Buying Ecosystem and the people or factors that may influence customer decisions.
Take a deeper look at the Buying Ecosystem and the different people, roles, and factors that influence purchasing decisions.
Explore the Job Process to understand the steps customers take to accomplish a specific job or goal.
Identify key stages, needs, and potential challenges within the customer’s process.
Apply these insights to build a more complete picture of your customer and their decision-making process.
What will you walk away knowing?
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to better map how your customer gets a job done and who (or what influences) their decisions along the way. These insights will help you identify opportunities and develop a stronger understanding of where your venture can provide differentiated value and solve your customer’s problem.

events.description:

Join the APIDA + Center and AANAPISI Initiatives for an inspiring evening with Dr. Kyle Reyes, a nationally recognized educator, advocate, and leader whose work centers on identity, belonging, leadership, and community impact. Whether you’re looking for inspiration, discovering your own advocacy journey, or simply interested in connecting with others, this is an evening you won’t want to miss.

Light refreshment served. Everyone is welcome!

events.title: Carrie Billy Public Lecture
events.description:
Join the Indigenous Community Center and the AANAPISI Initiative for a public lecture featuring Carrie Billy.

Billy will explore the interconnected importance of supporting Tribal students and strengthening Tribal sovereignty. Her talk will consider how creating meaningful pathways and support for Tribal students is deeply connected to recognizing, respecting, and advancing the sovereignty of Tribal nations.

This lecture offers an opportunity for students, faculty, staff, and community members to learn more about the relationship between Tribal education, student success, and Tribal sovereignty—and why supporting one strengthens the other.

All are welcome.

events.title: Thinking Thursday: Name, Image, and Whose Likeness: A Biblical Conversation about NIL, Identity, and Worth
events.description:
What is a college athlete worth— and who gets to decide? I’ll seek to explore how scripture helps us think about college sports, money, and the people at the center of the game. The question isn’t so much about what college athletes should be paid but what we are taught to prize.
Meet our speaker:
E.L. Smiling III is from Stafford, VA, and came to Virginia Tech in 2010 to study business marketing. He is the husband of Meghan Smiling and father of two boys, EL IV (4yo) and William (8mo.). During his time at VT, he was a Wide Receiver for the Hokies and is now the FCA campus director, the VT men’s basketball chaplain, and Worship Pastor at The Vine Church.

events.description:

Jumpstart is Magic's most beginner-friendly format, no deck-building required! You'll grab two themed booster packs, shuffle them together, and you're ready to play. Each pack comes with its own unique theme, creatures, and spells, so every game feels fresh and exciting. It's fast, fun, and a great way to experience what Magic is all about without any prior knowledge.

What to expect:
Free Jumpstart packs provided!
Casual, no-pressure gameplay for all skill levels
Experienced players on hand to teach rules and answer questions
A great opportunity to meet other Magic players at Virginia Tech
Stay and play as many rounds as you'd like

events.title: Venture Builders Workshop(Customer Discovery)
events.description:
What are Venture Builders Workshops?
Come meet other students interested in launching new ventures and develop new skills with Venture Builder’s Workshops.  Our workshops cover a variety of topics, including the exploration of customer problems through gathering first-person data, formation of actionable startup hypotheses, and how to validate those hypotheses through lightweight, technology-driven experiments—ultimately setting up our student entrepreneurs to build evidence-based ventures.
Not a student founder?  No problem. Whether you’re actively building a venture, are interested in joining a team, or just curious about entrepreneurship, all are welcome! 
What purpose do these workshops fulfill?
Each workshop connects to a specific incubator module, with an emphasis on learning concepts by putting them into practice, giving students the opportunity to explore key concepts, ask questions, and better understand the material.

What will this workshop be about?
This Workshop dives into Customer Discovery and focuses on how to learn directly from potential customers through effectively structured, problem-focused conversations.
During this workshop, you will:
Get an introduction to Customer Discovery and its role in understanding and validating customer problems.
Learn how to conduct problem-centric interviews that uncover meaningful customer insights.
Learn how to develop a clear problem hypothesis to guide your customer discovery efforts.
Identify who you should talk to and begin building your Interview List.
Use the Interview Form to prepare for and structure your customer conversations.
What will you walk away knowing?
By the end of the workshop, you’ll know how to develop a problem hypothesis, identify the “right” people to interview that align with your hypothesis, and conduct problem-centric conversations that help you learn from potential customers. You’ll also be better prepared to use your interview findings to evaluate your assumptions and guide the next steps for your venture.

events.title: Something Sapphic: Carabiner Craft Night
events.description:
Bring your own or get a new one, we'll be decorating & adorning our carabiners with key chains, stamped metal tags, and beads while we learn about queer women's fashion, iconography, and history!⁠
⁠
This event offers a hands-on educational experience that aims to raise awareness and understanding of sapphic culture and community. Queer and trans women make up a notable portion of the LGBTQ+ community, but they face misogyny both inside and outside of queer and trans spaces. As such, sapphic community and culture has been widely underrepresented in popular culture, public spaces, and history. This event aims to fill that gap by offering a lesson on queer women’s fashion, iconography, and history of queer flagging. Participants will be invited to decorate their own carabiner as a take-away from the event. This event is open to all, and all are welcome to engage in discussion and crafting.⁠
⁠
For more information or to request an accommodation, contact Haleigh Wallace at haleighwallace@vt.edu.

events.title: Chili Challenge at D2
events.description:
Is your palate fireproof? See if you can Tame the Flame in this year's Chili Challenge competition in D2's East Flex Room October 12th-16th from 12pm-6pm! Compete in a 5 day challenge where everyday you must eat and finish a bowl of chili. However, each day the chili grows hotter until the final day that will test even the strongest of palates. Starting from jalapeños to blazing with the Carolina reaper, sign up and complete the challenge to gain a unique Chili Challenge t-shirt. 

Rules:

Daily Commitment: You must eat one bowl of chili each day, Monday through Friday, between 12-6 p.m. to remain in the challenge. Skipping a day results in automatic disqualification.
Location & Check-In: You must eat in the designated Chili Challenge area and bring your event lanyard every day.
Verification: A judge must inspect and verify your completely finished bowl each day before you leave the area.
Beverages: Only plain water is permitted while eating. No milk, dairy, or outside drinks are allowed.
Prize: Everyone who successfully completes all 5 days will receive an exclusive Chili Challenge t-shirt.
 
You confirm that you are participating voluntarily, are in good health, and agree not to hold Virginia Tech Dining Services responsible for any physical reactions or aftereffects.

Are you looking for a way to unwind, recharge, and strengthen your mind-body connection? Senior Capstone students from the Adaptive Brain and Behavior Minor are presenting an enriching series of mindfulness-based practices designed to help you destress and recharge!

10/21- Topic- Focus- you will practice visualization

events.title: Founders Roundtable: Connect, Collaborate & Share
events.description:
What are Founders Roundtables?
Founders Roundtables are casual, conversational gatherings for startup founders, students exploring ideas, and anyone interested in connecting with the startup community. You don’t need to have a startup to join—just come ready to connect, share, learn, and enjoy pizza.
What is the purpose?
These roundtables create a space to build connections and spark collaboration. Founders can share their experiences, find potential team members, and get new perspectives, while students can discover startups to join and learn directly from those building ventures.
What can you expect?
Meet founders and students interested in startups.
Hear about founders’ journeys, challenges, and lessons learned.

events.title: KickStart
events.description:
What is KickStart?
KickStart is a dedicated opportunity for teams in the Apex Incubator to share updates on their startup progress as they move through key milestones in the Incubator roadmap. The event is also open to students and faculty who want to observe, learn about the startups, and connect with participating teams.
What is the purpose?
KickStart helps teams communicate where they are, what they’ve accomplished, and what they need to move forward. For teams facing funding-related barriers, it also provides an opportunity to request funding that can help unlock their next milestone.
What can you expect?
During KickStart, teams will:
Share updates on their startup progress and milestones achieved.
Present their next milestone or priority on the Incubator roadmap.
Identify challenges or funding barriers that may be blocking progress.
Explain what funding is needed for and how it will be used to advance their startup.
Connect with students, faculty, and others interested in their work.
Who should attend?
Apex Incubator teams, students, and faculty are welcome! Incubator teams can present their progress and funding needs, while other attendees can observe the presentations, learn about startups being built at Apex, and connect with the teams.

events.title: Founders Roundtable: Connect, Collaborate & Share
events.description:
What are Founders Roundtables?
Founders Roundtables are casual, conversational gatherings for startup founders, students exploring ideas, and anyone interested in connecting with the startup community. You don’t need to have a startup to join—just come ready to connect, share, learn, and enjoy pizza.
What is the purpose?
These roundtables create a space to build connections and spark collaboration. Founders can share their experiences, find potential team members, and get new perspectives, while students can discover startups to join and learn directly from those building ventures.
What can you expect?
Meet founders and students interested in startups.
Hear about founders’ journeys, challenges, and lessons learned.
Share ideas and get perspectives from others.
Find potential co-founders, team members, or collaborators.
Discover opportunities to join or contribute to a startup.
Connect in a relaxed, informal setting.
Who should attend?
Anyone interested in startups and entrepreneurship! Whether you’re building a venture, looking to join one, exploring an idea, or simply curious, Founders Roundtables are a place to connect, collaborate, and get involved.

events.title: Hokies Serve Saturday: Halloween @ Historic Smithfield
events.description:
Hokies Serve Saturdays are one-time volunteer opportunities that take place across the New River Valley.

When you participate, you'll:
• Learn about local issues and the organizations working to address them.
• Build meaningful connections with fellow Hokies.
• Make a tangible impact on community-identified priorities.

Held on weekends, Hokies Serve Saturdays are designed to fit into busy student schedules, making it easy to get involved without conflicting with classes or other weekday commitments.

October's community partner organization will be Historic Smithfield (1000 Merry Oak Way, Blacksburg, VA 24060). Volunteers will primarily assist with our hands-on, history-inspired crafts and demonstrations. No prior experience is necessary, we'll provide all the training they need. Activities may include helping visitors make grapevine wreaths, dip candles, create Halloween masks, make cornhusk dolls, or sculpt blacksmith-themed keepsakes from air-dry clay. We also need volunteers to staff our Welcome Booth, where they will greet visitors, distribute programs, and help count attendance at the gate. 

Volunteers have options to serve the morning shift, afternoon shift, or all day. Arrival times will be communicated in the sign up. 

Volunteers are encouraged to either come in a family friendly costume or utilize any available historic period clothing that is available at Historic Smithfield. 

Transportation will NOT be provided for this event due to proximity to campus! All volunteers must arrive early to their shift to be on time. 

Questions? Email rtjohnson@vt.edu.

events.title: Mind Body Flow
events.description:
Join Our Inclusive Mind Body Flow Program! 
Are you looking for a way to unwind, recharge, and strengthen your mind-body connection? Senior Capstone students from the Adaptive Brain and Behavior Minor are presenting an enriching series of mindfulness-based practices designed to help you destress and recharge!  

Whether you are new to mindfulness or you have some experience, this six-week journey is the perfect opportunity to explore various practices that can enhance your overall well-being. 

What to Expect: 

Our Mind Body Flow sessions offer a variety of practices that will help you relax, focus, and recharge for the busy weeks ahead:
10/7- Topic- How to be in the present, Practice-Body Scan
10/14- Topic- Awareness- you will learn to practice Mindfulness
10/21- Topic- Focus- you will practice visualization
10/28- Topic- Comfort- you will practice guided breath awareness
11/4- Topic- Overcoming obstacles- you will practice mindful communication
11/11- Topic- Digital Wellbeing- you will practice digital wellbeing

events.title: Venture Builders Workshop (Designing Small Experiments)
events.description:
What are Venture Builders Workshops?
Come meet other students interested in launching new ventures and develop new skills with Venture Builder’s Workshops.  Our workshops cover a variety of topics, including the exploration of customer problems through gathering first-person data, formation of actionable startup hypotheses, and how to validate those hypotheses through lightweight, technology-driven experiments—ultimately setting up our student entrepreneurs to build evidence-based ventures.
Not a student founder?  No problem. Whether you’re actively building a venture, are interested in joining a team, or just curious about entrepreneurship, all are welcome! 
What purpose do these workshops fulfill?
Each workshop connects to a specific incubator module, with an emphasis on learning concepts by putting them into practice, giving students the opportunity to explore key concepts, ask questions, and better understand the material.
What will this workshop be about?
This Workshop teaches effective techniques for Customer Validation and focuses on moving from customer discovery to testing your assumptions and gathering evidence by launching an Initial Product Release (IPR) to determine whether the customer problem you’ve identified is supported by data and behavior.
During this workshop, you will:
Learn the fundamentals of Customer Validation and hypothesis testing.
Explore how to run small, low-tech experiments called Initial Product Releases (IPR) to test your assumptions.
Learn how to connect your problem, hypothesis, and evidence to evaluate what you’ve learned.
Analyze insights and evidence gathered on your way to 30 live customer interviews.
Use the Experiment Results Analysis to evaluate and document your findings.
Note: post validation work, teams are eligible for  KickStart VT and the next stage of venture development + equity-free funding $.
What will you walk away knowing?
By the end of the workshop, you’ll understand how to test your assumptions, evaluate evidence, and determine what your customers are telling you (not just qualitatively, but quantitatively). You’ll be better prepared to use real-world feedback to validate—or challenge—your hypotheses and make informed decisions about the direction of your venture.

events.title: Venture Builders Workshop (Building an MVP)
events.description:
What are Venture Builders Workshops?
Come meet other students interested in launching new ventures and develop new skills with Venture Builder’s Workshops.  Our workshops cover a variety of topics, including the exploration of customer problems through gathering first-person data, formation of actionable startup hypotheses, and how to validate those hypotheses through lightweight, technology-driven experiments—ultimately setting up our student entrepreneurs to build evidence-based ventures.
Not a student founder?  No problem. Whether you’re actively building a venture, are interested in joining a team, or just curious about entrepreneurship, all are welcome! 
What purpose do these workshops fulfill?
Each workshop connects to a specific incubator module, with an emphasis on learning concepts by putting them into practice, giving students the opportunity to explore key concepts, ask questions, and better understand the material.
What will this workshop be about?
This Workshop covers Building Your 1st Minimum Viable Product (MVP) and focuses on turning what you’ve learned about your customers' problem and behaviors into a simple, testable MVP that can help you gather real-world evidence and begin proving demand.
During this workshop, you will:
Explore how starting with services can be a simple and effective way to test your venture idea.
Learn about the 1-Hour MVP and how to quickly turn an idea into something you can put in front of potential customers.
Explore ways to prove demand and determine whether customers are willing to engage with your offering.
Prepare to launch a live MVP experiment and document the results using the Experiment Results Analysis.
Continue strengthening your customer evidence through live interviews and ongoing customer discovery.
Explore how your ventures progress can help establish eligibility to apply for national competitions through the Apex Center’s Venture Founder’s program. 
What will you walk away knowing?
By the end of the workshop, you’ll understand how to move from customer insights to a simple, testable MVP. You’ll know how to launch an early experiment, measure customer response, and use the evidence you gather to determine whether there is real demand for your venture - before committing extensive amounts of time or money.

events.description:
Join Our Inclusive Mind Body Flow Program! 
Are you looking for a way to unwind, recharge, and strengthen your mind-body connection? Senior Capstone students from the Adaptive Brain and Behavior Minor are presenting an enriching series of mindfulness-based practices designed to help you destress and recharge!  

Whether you are new to mindfulness or you have some experience, this six-week journey is the perfect opportunity to explore various practices that can enhance your overall well-being. 

What to Expect: 

Our Mind Body Flow sessions offer a variety of practices that will help you relax, focus, and recharge for the busy weeks ahead:
10/7- Topic- How to be in the present, Practice-Body Scan
10/14- Topic- Awareness- you will learn to practice Mindfulness
10/21- Topic- Focus- you will practice visualization
10/28- Topic- Comfort- you will practice guided breath awareness
11/4- Topic- Overcoming obstacles- you will practice mindful communication
11/11- Topic- Digital Wellbeing- you will practice digital wellbeing

events.title: Venture Builders Workshop (Refining Your MVP)
events.description:
What are Venture Builders Workshops?
Come meet other students interested in launching new ventures and develop new skills with Venture Builder’s Workshops.  Our workshops cover a variety of topics including, the exploration of customer problems through gathering first-person data, formation of actionable startup hypotheses, and how to validate those hypotheses through lightweight, technology-driven experiments—ultimately setting up our student entrepreneurs to build evidence-based ventures.
Not a student founder?  No problem. Whether you’re actively building a venture, are interested in joining a team, or just curious about entrepreneurship, all are welcome! 
What purpose do these workshops fulfill?
Each workshop connects to a specific incubator module, with an emphasis on learning concepts by putting them into practice, giving students the opportunity to explore key concepts, ask questions, and better understand the material.
What will this workshop be about?
This workshop teaches common tools and techniques for refining your Minimum Viable Product (MVP Iteration) and focuses on using the feedback and evidence you’ve gathered from customers who are using your solution to evaluate, refine, and improve your MVP.
During this workshop, you will:
Review what you’ve learned from your initial MVP experiment and customer interactions.
Use your Experiment Results Analysis to identify key findings and areas for improvement.
Make informed updates to your MVP based on customer feedback and evidence.
Continue customer discovery through live interviews to strengthen your understanding of customer needs.
Develop and document an updated version of your MVP for continued testing.
Discuss ways to prepare National Competition applications using the progress and evidence you’ve gathered.
What will you walk away knowing?
By the end of the workshop, you’ll understand how to use customer feedback and experimental evidence to make informed changes to your MVP. You’ll be better prepared to iterate on your venture, continue testing your assumptions, and build an MVP that more closely reflects what your customers need - all signs of early traction.

events.title: Mind Body Flow
events.description:
Join Our Inclusive Mind Body Flow Program! 
Are you looking for a way to unwind, recharge, and strengthen your mind-body connection? Senior Capstone students from the Adaptive Brain and Behavior Minor are presenting an enriching series of mindfulness-based practices designed to help you destress and recharge!  

Whether you are new to mindfulness or you have some experience, this six-week journey is the perfect opportunity to explore various practices that can enhance your overall well-being. 

What to Expect: 

Our Mind Body Flow sessions offer a variety of practices that will help you relax, focus, and recharge for the busy weeks ahead:
10/7- Topic- How to be in the present, Practice-Body Scan
10/14- Topic- Awareness- you will learn to practice Mindfulness
10/21- Topic- Focus- you will practice visualization
10/28- Topic- Comfort- you will practice guided breath awareness
11/4- Topic- Overcoming obstacles- you will practice mindful communication
11/11- Topic- Digital Wellbeing- you will practice digital wellbeing

events.title: KickStart
events.description:
What is KickStart?
KickStart is a dedicated opportunity for teams in the Apex Incubator to share updates on their startup progress as they move through key milestones in the Incubator roadmap. The event is also open to students and faculty who want to observe, learn about the startups, and connect with participating teams.
What is the purpose?
KickStart helps teams communicate where they are, what they’ve accomplished, and what they need to move forward. For teams facing funding-related barriers, it also provides an opportunity to request funding that can help unlock their next milestone.
What can you expect?
During KickStart, teams will:
Share updates on their startup progress and milestones achieved.
Present their next milestone or priority on the Incubator roadmap.
Identify challenges or funding barriers that may be blocking progress.
Explain what funding is needed for and how it will be used to advance their startup.
Connect with students, faculty, and others interested in their work.
Who should attend?
Apex Incubator teams, students, and faculty are welcome! Incubator teams can present their progress and funding needs, while other attendees can observe the presentations, learn about startups being built at Apex, and connect with the teams.

events.title: Venture Builders Workshop (Creative Problem Solving)
events.description:
What are Venture Builders Workshops?
Come meet other students interested in launching new ventures and develop new skills with Venture Builder’s Workshops.  Our workshops cover a variety of topics including, the exploration of customer problems through gathering first-person data, formation of actionable startup hypotheses, and how to validate those hypotheses through lightweight, technology-driven experiments—ultimately setting up our student entrepreneurs to build evidence-based ventures.
Not a student founder?  No problem. Whether you’re actively building a venture, are interested in joining a team, or just curious about entrepreneurship, all are welcome! 
What purpose do these workshops fulfill?
Each workshop connects to a specific incubator module, with an emphasis on learning concepts by putting them into practice, giving students the opportunity to explore key concepts, ask questions, and better understand the material.
What will this workshop be about?
This Workshop will cover Creative Problem Solving (CPS) and how it can help you approach challenges from new perspectives.
During this workshop, you will:
Get an introduction to Creative Problem Solving (CPS) and its role in refining your core startup thesis. 
Participate in a hands-on CPS exercise using sample student problems.
Explore problems from different perspectives and identify new potential approaches.
Apply insights from the exercise to update and refine your Lean Business Model Canvas (LBMC).
What will you walk away knowing?
By the end of the workshop, you’ll know how to use Creative Problem Solving techniques to examine challenges, generate new possibilities, and make more informed decisions as you develop your venture.

events.title: All in Friday: See the Bigger Picture of Your Startup
events.description:
What are All-in-Fridays?
All-in-Fridays brings everything together. These 90-minute jam sessions provide a holistic view of the venture-building journey, helping you see how entrepreneurship content, activities, and deliverables connect across your startup’s development.  
Not a student founder?  No problem. Whether you’re actively building a venture, are interested in joining a team, or just curious about entrepreneurship, all are welcome! 
What purpose do All In Fridays fulfill?
All In Fridays give you a bird’s-eye view of the startup development process. Rather than focusing on one specific concept, these sessions help you step back, look at your venture as a whole, and understand where you are within the broader startup roadmap.
They are designed to help you connect your past work, current progress, and future priorities while identifying areas that may need more attention.
What will this All In Friday be about?
During this session, you will:
Explore the startup roadmap and see how our Canvas course incubator modules connect to the larger venture-building process.
Review your startup’s progress across different areas rather than focusing on a single incubator module.
Connect the work you’ve already completed with what you’re currently working on and what comes next.
Identify gaps or areas you haven’t explored yet within your venture.
Recognize which areas of your startup may need additional research, validation, or development.
Use the bigger picture to help determine where to focus your time and effort moving forward.
What will you walk away knowing?
By the end of All In Friday, you’ll have a clearer bird’s-eye view of your startup’s past, present, and future. You’ll better understand how the different pieces of your venture connect, where gaps may exist, and what next steps you should prioritize as you continue moving your startup forward.

---
